RE-REVIEW REQUEST — VERSION 2.2.0

Please re-review rio-metropolitan following the implemented changes in version 2.2.0. The previous review in #10682 / #10680 assigned approximately 0.33 / Low.

RESIDENT POPULATION AND WORKERS

Population remains based on the 2022 Census: 11,491,836 residents inside the map, without projecting total population to 2026.

Measured Census age-15–59 counts by census sector determine fine-scale worker weights. These are calibrated using Census 2022 municipal employed-resident estimates and then PNAD Contínua 2026Q2 occupation controls for the capital, metropolitan remainder and other covered areas.

The fine-scale source is therefore a working-age proxy, not measured employed residents at each building or census sector. Suppressed demographic cells affect approximately 0.697% of represented population and use an explicit municipal age-share fallback.

Original sector population totals and aggregation lineage are preserved. CNEFE 2022 dwelling units improve residential anchor locations, supporting approximately 99.23% of represented population. Where usable addresses are unavailable, the previous anchor is retained and reported. CNEFE addresses are not an authoritative building cadastre or measured per-building occupancy.

WORKPLACE DATA

RAIS 2024 establishment microdata are now the main source of formal employment geography throughout the covered municipalities. Active employment relationships are aggregated by registered municipality, CEP and CNAE/activity.

CNEFE non-residential address units provide candidate workplace locations. Establishment species and activity classifications are complemented by OSM/Overture building use, footprint area and height. RAIS postal/activity totals calibrate allocation weights across 19 activity classes.

This is an aggregate postal/activity allocation, not a shared-ID match between individual RAIS establishments and CNEFE addresses. Registered addresses are not claimed as verified physical workplaces.

Approximately 85.3% of formal links have postal support; 14.7% require municipal fallback. About 9.7% of all links have postal address extents exceeding 5 km. Exact matching methods, candidate counts, postal extents and fallback proportions are reported.

I conservatively selected municipal workplace granularity. Please assess whether the observed CEP/activity magnitudes across the covered municipalities justify an intermediate ADM4 classification, taking those limitations into account.

CEMPRE 2024 remains a separate municipal comparison. RAIS employment relationships, CEMPRE personnel and PNAD employed people have different statistical universes and are not added as interchangeable counts.

INFORMAL EMPLOYMENT

PNAD Contínua 2026Q2 metropolitan microdata provide weighted informal activity proportions. The calculated informality rate is approximately 37.83%, consistent with the published 37.8% control.

Fine activity splits within broad PNAD groups use RAIS composition as an explicit proxy. Informal destinations use compatible establishment addresses; domestic work and construction use residential support. These locations remain modeled, not observed informal workplaces.

COMMUTING

Municipal origin–destination quotas are determined before fine-scale workplace selection.

Census 2022 Table 10329 constrains local work outside the home and other-workplace categories. The public 2022 person microdata inspected do not expose the municipality identifiers required to construct a current pairwise OD matrix.

Other-municipality destination structure therefore uses an explicitly historical Census 2010 sample-expanded OD prior. This is not an observed 2022 pair matrix and not an enumerated OD matrix.

The model separately accounts for home workers, foreign/multiple workplaces and estimated destinations outside the map. External inbound workers are omitted. Estimated employed residents total 5,519,167; 4,414,637 generate in-map work trips.

Local containment is enforced. Initial destination weights are reconciled where necessary to make the closed model feasible; original source counts and all target adjustments remain in the reports.

IPF and integral residual-network rounding preserve municipal OD quotas and modeled workplace capacities exactly. Road-time gravity then disaggregates the fixed municipal quotas among workplace points. Directed OSM road paths determine driving distances and times, with explicit access connectors. Congestion is not modeled.

VALIDATION AND PLACEMENT CLASSIFICATION

The implementation uses 8,650 source demand points. Large workplace points aggregate multiple addresses; their modeled capacities are not verified individual-building capacities.

Validation reports include population preservation, employed-versus-commuter accounting, RAIS/CEMPRE comparisons, postal fallbacks, municipal OD targets and realized flows, historical differences, travel-time diagnostics and spatial outlier warnings. All 676 municipal OD pairs close exactly to their modeled targets.

The placement dropdowns use the closest conservative options available. Workplace allocation additionally uses CNEFE establishment addresses and locally calibrated RAIS postal/activity totals. Residential placement preserves measured census-sector counts and uses CNEFE dwelling addresses to select anchors.

Please assess the appropriate resolution and intensity classifications using the linked methodology, proposed answers and validation reports. No authoritative building cadastre or measured per-building employee counts are claimed.

Special passenger, visitor and student demand is separate from employment and excluded from the data-quality argument. No higher tier is claimed as already awarded.
